messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered (PD #INC-8421) — high connection usage: redis-main maxclients ~97% and pgbouncer total_conn ~92%. Auto-page to eng-oncall and infra-leads.

maya: seeing huge spike in reads + tx bursts from model-serving-svc. KV cache miss storms on a few prefixes. Clients piling up.

aj: acked. jumping in. any impact to user-facing endpoints?

maya: some 503s on /v1/generate and slow tails on chat streams. Token latency up 2-3x. Root cause looks like simultaneous prefix cache invalidations + a large reporting job hitting the DB.

samir: i'm on pgbouncer dashboard — most servers at pool saturation, queueing. Pg replicas are fine but primary has connection queueing.

olivia: paging DB on-call (pd escalation) and opening runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-conn-spike. can someone check if pgbouncer max_client_conn is set too low for this release?

aj: running quick mitigation — scaling pgbouncer and temporarily increasing pool_size.

aj: ```shell
kubectl -n infra scale deploy pgbouncer --replicas=4
# increase per-pool limits via configmap patch if scale doesn't absorb
```

maya: starting a small canary rollback of the recent model rollout (rollout id mr-2026-09-12) to reduce request fanout to cache.

incident-bot: PagerDuty note — alert acknowledged by aj at 2371112232. Escalation schedule unchanged.

samir: while pgbouncer scales, we can offload non-critical analytics traffic to the read-replica cluster and flip report-job to delayed queue. running SQL kill on the long-running query (reporting_export) that's holding ~60 ephemeral connections.

olivia: executed kill pid 42312 on primary, confirmed freed 60 conns. watching queue length.

maya: redis cluster also seeing blocked clients due to client output buffer growth. increasing maxclients buy us time but need to consider prefix-based cache partitioning to avoid hotkey bursts.

aj: patched redis config for ephemeral increase: ```redis-cli CONFIG SET maxclients 12000``` then bounced the proxy pods. clients dropping slowly.

samir: pg queue length down from 150 -> 12. pgbouncer replicas hot but handling it. monitoring 1m and 5m error rates.

maya: product impact assessment: roughly 8% of requests got 5xx during peak 2371112223-2371112255, mostly short-lived. billing-affecting? no. SLA blips logged.

olivia: documenting mitigation timeline in PD incident and adding postmortem checklist items: adjust pgbouncer autoscale policy, add prefix-aware cache warming, and add guard for simultaneous model-rollouts that touch same keyspace.

aj: handing off to samir for watch and cleanup. samir, can you keep it monotored for 30m and then hand to daytime oncall? i'll update the incident thread with actions. :thumbsup:

samir: taking over. will keep watch and post updates; planning to revert temporary cfg changes after 45m if stable.

pagerduty-bot: PD INC-8421 status: acknowledged -> mitigation in progress -> owner: aj -> next: samir.

maya: thanks all. filing notes for postmortem. if it looks healthy in 45m we can close the PD.

samir: last check at 2371112339: error rate down to baseline, redis maxclients ~60%, pgbouncer queue ~0-3. marking incident as recovering.

incident-bot: incident resolved? please confirm by closing PD or marking as resolved in this thread.
